200.q: I have hands but cannot clap. I have a face but no eyes. What am I?
I am tall when young and short when old. You burn me to light the dark. What am I?
I have keys but no locks. I have space but no room. You can enter but not go inside. What am I?
The more you take, the more you leave behind. What am I?
I speak without a mouth and hear without ears. I have no body but I come alive with wind. What am I?
What has four legs but doesn't walk?
What must be broken before you can use it?
The more I dry, the wetter I get. What am I?
What goes up but never comes down?
I have cities but no houses. I have mountains but no trees. I have water but no fish. What am I?
I have an eye but cannot see. I am small and pointy. What am I?
I follow you all day but disappear when night falls. What am I?
I have a head and a tail but no body. What am I?
I have a neck but no head. I may be filled with drink. What am I?
I have many teeth but cannot bite. I help neaten your hair. What am I?
I can travel around the world while staying in a corner. What am I?
I run but never walk. I have a bed but never sleep. What am I?
I have a thumb and four fingers but I am not alive. What am I?
I am full of holes but still hold water. What am I?
I have roots no one sees. I am taller than trees. Up up I go and yet never grow. What am I?
I am always in front of you but can never be seen. What am I?
I have branches but no fruit, trunk, or leaves. You visit me to hold your money. What am I?
The more you have of me, the less you see. What am I?
I have one head, one foot, and four legs. Each night you sleep on me. What am I?
I am so fragile that saying my name breaks me. What am I?
Until I am measured, I am not known, yet you miss me when I have flown. What am I?
I have teeth but cannot eat. I keep clothes closed. What am I?
I can fly without wings and cry without eyes. I drift across the sky. What am I?
I have 13 hearts but no organs. I am shuffled and dealt. What am I?
I grow short the more I am used. I have wood but am not a tree. What am I?
I reflect what stands before me, yet I have no eyes. I break into bad luck. What am I?
I am tall when new and short when old. You burn me for light. What am I?
I fall but never break. I break but never fall. What are we?
I have a ring but no finger. I chime or buzz. What am I?
I have a head at night and lose it during the day. What am I?
I am black inside and white outside. I am full of holes yet I hold. What am I?
I have leaves but am not a plant. I have a spine but no bones. What am I?
I am a glass box that holds water and creatures with gills. You feed my inhabitants flakes. What am I?
I have two hands but no arms. I strike every hour. What am I?
I freeze in cold and melt in heat, yet I cannot move. What am I?
I have wheels but no engine. I race down hills on snow. What am I?
I am white and cold. I fall from the sky in flakes. What am I?
I come in pairs and live on feet. You lace me up. What am I?
I hold your tea and sit on a table. I have a handle and a lip. What am I?
I store all your clothes. I have drawers but no pens. What am I?
I ring, I buzz, or I sing. I wake you up in the morning. What am I?
I flutter in the breeze and tell the nation's story. What am I?
I have petals but no voice. I smell sweet to lovers. What am I?
I hop in the grass and was once a tadpole. What am I?
I am round and citrus-colored, named after my own hue. You squeeze me for juice. What am I?
I am long and yellow and monkeys love me. What am I?
I hold scissors, erasers, rulers and writing tools on a student's desk. What am I?
I shine at night but hide by day. I change shape every month. What am I?
I am the brightest in the sky and warm your skin. What am I?
I fall from the sky and water the garden. What am I?
I am a plastic or metal vessel you refill at the fountain. Runners carry me with a strap. What am I?
I have a point at one end and an eraser at the other. What am I?
I beep in the kitchen when food is ready. What am I?
I connect two floors and I can be made of wood or stone. What am I?
I grow taller by the year but I do not breathe. I have bark but cannot bite. What am I?
I have a lid but no mouth. I open to reveal a meal. What am I?
I spin and cool a room without giving a breeze from nature. What am I?
I open when the sky closes in and fold away when it clears. When the wind flips me inside out, I've lost the fight. What am I?
I have two blades that are useless apart; I only cut when my legs cross. What am I?
I have bristles and visit your mouth twice a day, yet I never taste a thing. What am I?
I have many rungs but no bell, and I take you higher while standing perfectly still. What am I?
Feed me air and I grow; poke me and I go out with a bang. What am I?
I fly only when I'm tied down, dancing with the wind on the end of a string. What am I?
I bite paper and leave two tiny metal teeth behind to hold the pages together. What am I?
I hum all day and keep a bulb that only shines when you open my door. What am I?
I have four tines and a handle, and I spear your dinner on its way to your mouth. What am I?
I hug your waist and have a row of holes so I can loosen as you grow. What am I?
I have a tongue that swings but cannot taste, and I only speak when struck. What am I?
I have one round foot and two arms the gardener holds, and I haul dirt and stones. What am I?
I have a head and a claw but no body, and I drive nails home. What am I?
I have a skin but no body, and I only sing when beaten. What am I?
I have a long handle and stiff bristles, and I chase dust across the floor. What am I?
I have a mouth that swallows letters and a little flag that goes up when I've been fed. What am I?
I have a glass head and a glowing wire heart, and I wake at the flick of a switch. What am I?
I stand all day in a field with my arms stretched wide, and the birds never trust me. What am I?
When one end of me goes up, the other must come down; two children ride me at the park. What am I?
I wear spines instead of leaves and can wait months between drinks. What am I?
I am a house you carry on your back and raise before dark. What am I?
I have twelve pages and hundreds of numbers, and you throw me away every January. What am I?
I rise when you have a fever and fall when it freezes, though I have no legs. What am I?
I have a needle that never sews, and it always searches for the same direction. What am I?
I have two wheels and no engine, and I only stay upright while we're moving. What am I?
I have three eyes stacked one above another, and drivers obey whichever one is open. What am I?
I make the brightest day look dim and hide your eyes from the crowd. What am I?
I fold in half, live in your pocket, and hold your cards and cash. What am I?
I start as a hard little kernel and burst into a fluffy white puff when heated. What am I?
Children build me with a bucket and a spade, and the tide takes me back every evening. What am I?
I have a head but no brain, and I get pounded into wood to do my job. What am I?
I have six strings and a hollow body, and I sing when strummed. What am I?
I sleep for centuries, then wake and spit fire from my top. What am I?
I am born in winter with a carrot for a nose, and I disappear when spring comes. What am I?
I catch the wind so a boat can move, though I have no engine at all. What am I?
I hold your place while you're away, tucked between the pages. What am I?
I take away mistakes and grow smaller with every one I fix. What am I?
I stand over water with my feet on both banks, and cars drive across my back. What am I?
I stand alone on the rocks and blink all night so ships keep their distance. What am I?
I have teeth but never bite, and I get pulled up and down all day. What am I?
I have four legs and a back, but I'm the one who gets sat on. What am I?
I have bark but never bite, and my rings give away how old I am. What am I?
I have a stem and a bowl, but I'm not a flower and I hold no soup. What am I?
I have a bridge but no river, a neck but no head, and six strings. What am I?
I have blades but I'm not a knife, and I spin above your head to keep you cool. What am I?
I have a trunk and a hood but no face, and I spend the night in the driveway. What am I?
I have ribs but no heart, and I only open when the rain comes. What am I?
I have a mouth and a neck but no head, and I hold flowers. What am I?
I have a handle and a spout, and I whistle when I'm ready. What am I?
I have a tail and I fly, but only while you hold my string. What am I?
I have four strings, I'm played with a bow, and I'm tucked under your chin. What am I?
I have eyes but cannot see, and I'm dug up, mashed, and fried. What am I?
I have a head but never think, and my head is nothing but foam. What am I?
I have teeth along my edge, and I cut wood by going back and forth. What am I?
I have a tongue but never taste, and my ringing calls people to church. What am I?
I have springs but no water, and I bounce you into the air. What am I?
I have a deck but no cards, a bow but no arrow, and a stern that's never angry. What am I?
I have a brim but no cup, and I sit on top of your head. What am I?
I have a collar but no neck, and sleeves but no arms. What am I?
I have a heel and a toe but no foot of my own, and I often lose my twin in the wash. What am I?
I have leaves but no branches, and I'm steeped in hot water. What am I?
I have a thumb but no fingers, and I keep your hand warm. What am I?
I have a foot but no leg, and I keep your lines straight. What am I?
I have a seat but no legs, and I hang from a branch on two ropes. What am I?
I have a spout, and I rain on the flowers whenever you tip me. What am I?
I have a head, and I only light up when I'm struck. What am I?
I always point north but never travel anywhere. What am I?
I'm knocked on but never hurt, and answered though I never ask a question. What am I?
I have a bridge but no river, and two arms that hook behind your ears. What am I?
I have a lip but never speak, a handle but never grab, and I hold your morning coffee. What am I?
I have a crust, a mantle, and a core, but I'm not a pie. What am I?
I'm built into a house; you climb me to go up and climb me to come down, but I never move an inch. What am I?
I have a cap but no head and gills but I'm no fish, and I pop up after rain. What am I?
I have wings but no feathers, and I carry hundreds of people without flapping once. What am I?
I fly by night but I'm no bird, and I also hit home runs. What am I?
I have a bridge but cross no water, and I can run without legs. What am I?
I have a pupil but I'm no teacher, and lids but I'm no jar. What am I?
I have two slots, I turn bread golden brown, and I pop when I'm done. What am I?
I have a slot for a mouth, I swallow letters, and I stand by the door or out by the road. What am I?
I have two blades that cross, and I only work when I'm opened and closed. What am I?
I'm a roof on a stick, and you only remember me when it rains. What am I?
I have a tail and I dance in the wind, but only when someone holds my line. What am I?
I'm full of air, I'm tied to a string, and a pin is my worst enemy. What am I?
I have rungs instead of stairs, and I lean on walls for a living. What am I?
I have a bristly head and a long handle, and I sweep up what nobody else will. What am I?
I have a bowl at one end and a handle at the other, and soup is hopeless without me. What am I?
I have prongs instead of fingers, and I stab your dinner for you. What am I?
I'm worn in pairs, I hide inside your shoes, and one of me always vanishes in the wash. What am I?
I hold up your trousers with a buckle, and I have many holes but use only one at a time. What am I?
I'm black, round and rubbery, and I go flat at the worst possible moment. What am I?
I have a door and a light that comes on when you open me, and I hum all night. What am I?
I'm a box that heats your food in seconds, and metal is not allowed inside me. What am I?
I'm a small flat disc with holes in the middle, and I keep your shirt from falling open. What am I?
I have shoulders but no arms, and I wear your clothes while you're not. What am I?
I lie by the front door, you wipe your feet on me, and I often say 'Welcome'. What am I?
I'm a bent piece of wire that holds papers together without piercing them. What am I?
I have a bowl but hold no soup, a seat but I'm no chair, and I'm flushed every day. What am I?
I have a head but never think, and I rain on you indoors every morning. What am I?
I hang from the ceiling, I'm covered in tiny mirrors, and I spin while people dance. What am I?
I have a bell and two wheels, and I go nowhere without your legs. What am I?

400.q: I am lighter than a feather, yet the strongest person cannot hold me for long. What am I?
I can hide a whole city, but I am made of tiny drops. The more of me there is, the less you see. What am I?
What can you catch but not throw?
I can be cracked, told, or played. People laugh when they hear me. What am I?
What 5-letter word becomes shorter when you add two letters to it?
What belongs to you, but other people use it more than you do?
I have many keys but open no locks. I make music instead. What am I?
What has four wheels and flies?
What can two people have without ever touching it?
I am the beginning of everything and the end of everywhere. What am I?
A five-letter word that sounds the same after removing four of its letters. What is it?
Give me food and I will live. Give me water and I will die. What am I?
I have no voice but teach you much. I have spines and hinges but am not a plant or a door. What am I?
What begins with the letter e and ends with the letter e but only contains one letter?
What comes once in a minute, twice in a moment, but never in a thousand years?
What invention lets you look right through a wall?
You can see me in water, but I never get wet. What am I?
I begin and have no end. I am also the ending of all that begins. What am I?
I am a word of 5 letters. People eat me. Remove my first letter and I become a form of energy. What am I?
People buy me to eat but never eat me. What am I?
If you have me, you want to share me. If you share me, you don't have me. What am I?
What kind of tree can you carry in your hand?
What room do ghosts avoid?
I am not a plant but I have leaves. I am not royalty but I have a crown. I am sweet but sugar was never added. What am I?
You can hear me but never see me. I come out when you speak. What am I?
I can run but have no legs. I am on your face. What am I?
What invention allows you to walk through walls?
One of us breaks yet never falls. The other falls yet never breaks. What are we?
I keep ships from drifting. I sink but never drown. What am I?
I have an eye but cannot see. I can tear roofs from homes. What am I?
I begin with the letter E and end with the letter E, yet I contain just one letter. What am I?
I can run but have no legs. I sit between the eyes. What am I?
I have a spine but no legs. I sit on shelves for years. What am I?
I have a neck but no shoulders. I have a cap but no hair. What am I?
I am kept for life but cannot be held. I fade as one ages. What am I?
I'm black when you get me, red when you use me, and grey when you throw me away. What am I?
I can be quick or dead, yet never breathed. What am I?
I circle a finger as a symbol of lifelong love. I am often made of gold. What am I?
What comes down but never goes up?
I have a thousand needles but cannot sew. I grow in the mountains. What am I?
I travel from room to room without moving. I follow the pipes. What am I?
I am the only word that ends in MT. What am I?
I have a face with numbers, but no head with brains. I tick-tock. What am I?
I cover the bed but am neither sheet nor blanket. I am decorative. What am I?
You use me when you go from one floor to another, but I have no stairs. What am I?
I get wet while drying, and I hang in the bathroom. What am I?
I am a ship that sails underwater without getting wet inside. What am I?
I flash and crack across the sky, louder than a drum. What am I?
I bend light across the sky after rain. I have seven colors. What am I?
I live underground and rise only to bloom. I am wrapped in papery skin. What am I?
I have many rings but I am not for fingers. I float in soda. What am I?
I can be split or shared, yet never divided in half cleanly. I keep families bonded. What am I?
I lie at your feet and greet every arrival. What am I?
I have threads but no cloth, and a head that turns with a twist. What am I?
I take a hot bath, bleed my color into the water, and then get thrown away. What am I?
I lose my head the first time I'm used, and I'm useless after that. What am I?
I have six faces but wear no expression, and twenty-one dots but cannot see. What am I?
I am a single bent wire that holds pages together without leaving a hole. What am I?
I tell the truth every morning, and people step on me anyway. What am I?
I am a row of black stripes hiding a number, and I beep at the checkout. What am I?
I run through eyelets, get tied twice a day, and trip you when I'm loose. What am I?
No two of me are alike, and I'm left on everything you touch. What am I?
I only tell time when the sky is clear, with one hand that never moves. What am I?
I have a hole for a key but no key of my own, and I open for only one. What am I?
I am a throat on the roof that swallows only smoke. What am I?
Bury me and I rise; I am the smallest thing a forest needs. What am I?
I am beaten with a stick at parties, and everyone cheers when I burst. What am I?
Tie me and I hold; pull me the wrong way and I only tighten. What am I?
I carry your face across borders and collect stamps from strangers. What am I?
I show only a tenth of myself, and the rest of me sank a famous ship. What am I?
I take your money without a word and drop your snack from behind glass. What am I?
I am a creature turned to stone, sleeping in rock for millions of years. What am I?
I grow inside a living shell, born from a grain of sand, and end up on a necklace. What am I?
I twist and pull, and without me the wine stays trapped. What am I?
Tip me over and all my brothers fall in a line; I wear spots on my face. What am I?
My arms turn all day without lifting a thing, and I grind grain when the breeze blows. What am I?
I open only when you're falling, and the air is what fills me. What am I?
I am art that bleeds while it's made, and I stay with you for life. What am I?
I tick like a clock but tell no time, and I keep musicians in step. What am I?
I drop and climb back up a string, and I can sleep at the bottom of it. What am I?
I come in twice a day and go out twice a day, pulled by something I never touch. What am I?
I am a river of ice that moves too slowly to see. What am I?
I flash before my loud brother arrives, and I can split a tree in a blink. What am I?
I am the mark a blow leaves behind; I bloom purple, then fade to yellow. What am I?
I am contagious but no disease; see me and you'll probably give me back. What am I?
I force your eyes shut for a split second, and strangers bless you for it. What am I?
I pull without hands and push my own kind away. What am I?
I am the slow orange fire that eats iron without a flame. What am I?
I am a yellow weed that turns into a white wish you blow away. What am I?
I am a sliver of wood small enough to hide under skin and make a grown man wince. What am I?
I hang around a doctor's neck and let a stranger hear your heart. What am I?
I show your bones without cutting you open. What am I?
I have pupils but I'm not an eye, and a bell tells me when to start. What am I?
I have a crown but no throne, and a root but no leaves. What am I?
I have a shoulder but no arm, and I pass through towns without ever moving. What am I?
I was never alive, yet I can die, and when I do, everything I power goes dark. What am I?
I go in hard and come out soft, and you can blow me into a bubble. What am I?
I have an eye but cannot see, and I'm calm at my center while everything around me is wild. What am I?
I have a tail made of ice and dust, and I only grow it when I get close to the sun. What am I?
I'm the only kind of coat you put on while it's wet. What am I?
I'm taken, shot, and framed, but I've never committed a crime. What am I?
I can be caught but never thrown, and I'm most common in winter. What am I?
I'm drawn without a pencil, I run without legs, and I'm taken hot. What am I?
I run without legs and drop without falling, and the saddest people make the most of me. What am I?
I can be kept, given, and broken, but never touched. What am I?
I fly all day but never go anywhere. What am I?
I have a heel but no foot, and a crust but no dirt. What am I?
I'm full of dates but never go on one, and I'm thrown away every twelve months. What am I?
I have a fly but never buzz, and two legs but never walk. What am I?
I come in a hand but never on an arm, and monkeys can't get enough of me. What am I?
I have a drum and a canal, but no music and no boats. What am I?
I can be cast, broken, and lifted, and witches are famous for me. What am I?
I have a train but no tracks, and I'm usually worn only once. What am I?
I have an ear but cannot hear, and I'm dressed in silk and husk. What am I?
I'm drawn every evening, but never with a pencil, and I hide you from the street. What am I?
I'm held to keep you quiet and bitten to stop a remark. What am I?
I'm an insect, but I also crash your software. What am I?
I have a crown but I'm no king, and roots but I'm no tree. What am I?
I'm contagious but not a disease; just watching someone do me makes you do me too. What am I?
I come uninvited in little bursts, and people try to frighten me away. What am I?
People bless you the moment I arrive, and you can't keep your eyes open while I happen. What am I?
I've been with you since before you were born, and the day I stop is your last. What am I?
I'm the price of last night's fun, paid first thing the next morning. What am I?
Scratching me feels wonderful, but I always come back for more. What am I?
I'm a mistake you only notice after you've pressed send. What am I?
Read me forward or backward and I say exactly the same thing. What am I?
I'm a line you can always see but never reach, and I back away as fast as you approach. What am I?
I'm a shimmering lake in the desert that disappears the moment you arrive. What am I?
I'm what iron slowly turns into when water and air get at it. What am I?
I'm partly made of you, and I settle on everything you own the moment you stop cleaning. What am I?
I'm tiny, I come from wood, and I get right under your skin. What am I?
I'm a voice with the volume turned down, and secrets travel by me. What am I?
I'm made on birthday flames and falling stars, and telling me is said to spoil me. What am I?
I'm found on an elephant, on a tree, and at the back of a car. What am I?
I'm a bird with long legs, and I lift steel beams on building sites. What am I?
I grow on a palm, I'm a number on a calendar, and I'm an evening out with someone you like. What am I?
Two teams can finish in me, and you knot me around your neck. What am I?
I'm strapped to a wrist, and I'm also what a guard does all night. What am I?
I'm a season, a coil of metal, and a place where water bubbles up from the ground. What am I?
I'm twenty-five cents, fifteen minutes, and a fourth of a football game. What am I?
I hold ink for writing, and I hold pigs on a farm. What am I?
I'm a suit in a deck of cards, a tool for golf, and a place to dance all night. What am I?
I'm on a duck's face, in your wallet, and I arrive at the end of a meal. What am I?
I'm a fried potato, a sliver of silicon in your phone, and a token at a casino. What am I?
I'm baked with chocolate, and websites keep asking you to accept me. What am I?
I live under bridges in fairy tales and in comment sections online. What am I?
I'm a key on a keyboard, a page in your browser, and what you run up at a bar. What am I?
I'm on your front door, and I'm also a curl of your hair. What am I?
I'm a vaccine in your arm, a small glass of whiskey, and a basketball attempt. What am I?
Trains run on me, sprinters race around me, and I'm one song on an album. What am I?
I spin to keep you cool, and I scream at concerts. What am I?
I'm meat in a can, and I'm junk in your inbox. What am I?
I'm the smallest unit of life, a prisoner's room, and what Americans call their mobile phone. What am I?

600.q: Three lives have I. Gentle enough to soothe the skin, light enough to caress the sky, hard enough to crack rocks. What am I?
Two bodies have I, though both joined in one. The more still I stand, the quicker I run. What am I?
At night they come without being fetched, and by day they are lost without being stolen. What are they?
The man who makes me does not want me. The man who buys me does not use me. The man who uses me does not know it. What am I?
Always old, sometimes new. Never sad, sometimes blue. Never empty, sometimes full. What am I?
I make you weak at the worst of times. I make your heart pound and hands sweat. I visit the weak but seldom the bold. What am I?
A cloud is my mother, the wind is my father. A rainbow is my bed, the earth my final resting place. What am I?
I am the black child of a white father, a wingless bird flying even to the clouds of heaven. What am I?
He marries many women but has never been married himself. Who is he?
Alive without breath, as cold as death. Never thirsty, ever drinking. All in mail, never clinking. What am I?
I start with T, end with T, and have T in me. What am I?
What word in the dictionary is spelled incorrectly?
Voiceless it cries, wingless flutters, toothless bites, mouthless mutters. What is it?
I can be long or short. I can be grown or bought. I can be painted or left bare. I can be round or square. What am I?
The sun bakes them, the hand breaks them, the foot treads on them, and the mouth tastes them. What are they?
I turn once — that which is outside will not get in. I turn again — that which is inside will not get out. What am I?
I am the fountain from which no one can drink. Like gold to all I am sought. What am I?
What can fill a room but takes up no space?
I have no life, but I can die. You plug me in to charge. What am I?
What has three feet but cannot walk?
Poor people have it. Rich people need it. If you eat it, you die. What is it?
The more you take away from me, the bigger I grow. What am I?
I have a tongue but cannot taste, a sole but no soul. What am I?
What are the next two letters in the series: O, T, T, F, F, S, S, _, _?
A man rode into town on Friday, stayed three days, and left on Friday. How?
A mother had three children. The first was named April, the second May. What was the third child's name?
What is black when clean and white when dirty?
I get smaller every time I take a bath. What am I?
I am always coming but never arrive. What am I?
I have 64 squares, 32 pieces do battle on me. What am I?
A cloud is my mother, the wind my father. A rainbow is my bed, the earth my final resting place. What am I?
I have mountains, valleys, rivers and deserts but no soil, water or grass. What am I?
I have cities but no people. I have forests but no trees. I have rivers without water. What am I?
If you drop me I'm sure to crack, but give me a smile and I'll always smile back. What am I?
I have a shining head and a matching tail but a hollow middle. I am minted by kings. What am I?
What word looks the same upside down and backward?
I have no eyes, ears, or spine, but I tell a gripping story. I have many pages. What am I?
I run over fields and woods all day. Under the bed at night I sit not alone. My tongue hangs out, up and to the rear, awaiting to be filled in the morning. What am I?
I am taken from a mine and shut up in a wooden case, from which I am never released. Yet I am used by almost every person. What am I?
I am everywhere, but you can't see me. I fill lungs and lift kites. What am I?
I come in many shapes and colors. Snap me in half and I might shatter your teeth. What am I?
Every dawn begins with me. At dusk I'll be the first you see. Without me, planets would collapse. What am I?
I have a heart that never beats. I have a home but never sleep. I can take a man's house and build another's. And I love to play games with my many brothers. What am I?
I am an insect and half my name is another insect. I am similar to a creature which is called after a letter. What am I?
Forward I am heavy, backward I am not. What am I?
I have lakes with no water, mountains with no stone, and cities with no buildings. What am I?

I can sizzle like bacon, I am made with an egg, I have plenty of backbone but lack a good leg. I peel layers like onions but still remain whole. I can be long like a flagpole, yet fit in a hole. What am I?
I weaken all men for hours each day. I show you strange visions while you are away. I take you by night, by day take you back. None suffer to have me, but do from my lack. What am I?
I am easily made and easily broken; keeping me is the only hard part. What am I?
I travel fast, grow with every telling, and rarely arrive the way I left. What am I?
I am hard to make and harder to break, and I act before you decide. What am I?
The longer you keep me, the more of me there is, and I follow you until you pay. What am I?
I grow when you give me nothing and vanish when you give me something. What am I?
I'm easy to tell and hard to keep track of, and I need more of my kind to survive. What am I?
Alone I'm worth nothing, but stand me behind another number and I make it ten times bigger. What am I?
I am written by the winners and repeated by those who won't learn me. What am I?
I'm offered whenever I'm needed, and the more I'm used the less I'm believed. What am I?
I am held but have no handle, and carrying me hurts only the one who carries. What am I?
I am a virtue everyone needs but nobody wants to wait for. What am I?
I take years to build, seconds to break, and forever to repair. What am I?
The more attention you give me, the worse I get; ignore me and I fade. What am I?
I rise, curl, and crash on the shore, but I never bring the water with me; I'm just energy passing through. What am I?
I make the past look better than it ever was, and I ache sweetly. What am I?
I am the eerie feeling that you've lived this exact moment before, though you haven't. What am I?
I make your money worth less without taking a single note from your wallet. What am I?
I am cast but never caught, and counted but never spent. What am I?
I am a joke that earns a groan instead of a laugh, playing on two meanings at once. What am I?
I say the opposite of what I mean, and you know it only from my tone. What am I?
Shakespeare called me the green-eyed monster, and I grow when you compare yourself to others. What am I?
I happen thousands of times a day without your noticing, and I keep your eyes from drying out. What am I?
I promise to save you time, and I often cost you the most. What am I?
Everyone makes me, few admit me, and the wise learn from me. What am I?
I'm blamed when things go wrong and thanked when they go right, but I never planned any of it. What am I?
People work fastest just before I arrive, and I am often missed. What am I?
Read me backwards and I'm still the same; 'racecar' is one of me. What am I?
I am ruined the moment you hear about me. What am I?
I come at the very end, and without me the whole setup was for nothing. What am I?
Everyone has one of me; the wise keep me to themselves, and the loud can't. What am I?
I arrive before you and stay after you leave, and one bad day can ruin me. What am I?
I am made entirely of people trying to get somewhere, and I go nowhere. What am I?
I tell strangers where you're from before you say it, and you can't hear your own. What am I?
I hang from a cave's ceiling and grow one drip at a time. What am I?
I am water shimmering in the desert that was never really there. What am I?
I am a hot spring that loses its temper on schedule, throwing water at the sky. What am I?
I raise the hair on your arms when you're cold or scared, and I'm named after a plucked bird. What am I?
I stand on one leg with my heart in my head. What am I?
I have a foot on each end and one in the middle. What am I?
I wear a belt of three stars and hunt across the winter sky. What am I?
I break at dawn, I'm called at dusk, and heroes are always saving me. What am I?
I'm served in prison, and I end with a full stop. What am I?
I'm found at the end of every rainbow, though no gold sits beside me. What am I?
There are two of me in a corner, one in a room, none in a house, but one in a shelter. What am I?
I'm lost, kept, and held, and I go quickest in an argument. What am I?
I'm paid but never bought, caught but never thrown, and held but never touched. What am I?
I'm set, broken, and beaten, yet I never feel a thing. What am I?
I have a heart but no other organs, and I'm eaten leaf by leaf. What am I?
I'm a seven-letter word, yet I hold thousands of letters. What am I?
I'm a word for shining your shoes, but give me a capital letter and I become a nationality. What am I?
Most of me hides below the surface, I'm lighter than the water I came from, and ships fear me. What am I?
Flip me upside down and I'm worth half again as much. What am I?
I read the same forwards, backwards, and upside down, and I'm the middle of the day. What am I?
I'm a five-letter word you might skip across a pond; drop my first two letters and I become a number. What am I?
I come to you every night, but I'm usually gone by breakfast. What am I?
I'm the everyday English word with three sets of double letters in a row. What am I?
No matter how many times you add me to myself, I never grow. What am I?
Read me forward and I'm what everyone has done; read me backward and I'm someone you'd rather never meet. What am I?
Read me backward and I become the sweetest course of the meal. What am I?
The longer you hold me, the heavier I become, yet I weigh nothing at all. What am I?
I'm a secret only you should know, made of letters and numbers, and you forget me right when you need me most. What am I?
I'm yours alone, yet you give me away every time you agree to something in writing. What am I?
I rise to your cheeks when you'd rather hide, and no order can send me away. What am I?
I die the moment someone explains me. What am I?
I'm always on my way, I make you work harder the closer I get, and missing me costs you. What am I?
I'm the place you claim you were, and I'm only needed once you're suspected. What am I?
I'm a gap in the rules that lets people through without breaking any of them. What am I?
I follow you across oceans and make noon feel like midnight. What am I?
I'm a song whose success is measured by how fast my audience stops listening. What am I?
I'm what the crowd demands after the show has already ended. What am I?
I'm an ending that refuses to end, and I'm the reason you press 'next episode'. What am I?
I'm three little dots that say the most by saying nothing at all. What am I?
I cure nothing, yet I make people feel better simply because they believe I will. What am I?
I'm nothing at all, and nature is said to hate me. What am I?
I can be a string of words, or a stretch of years behind bars. What am I?
I'm a field for football, a throw in baseball, and how high or low a note sounds. What am I?
I'm a mark that means yes, a way to pay someone, and a threat to a king in chess. What am I?
I hold your dishes in the kitchen, and I advise a president. What am I?
I'm a country's main city, an uppercase letter, and the money you need to start a business. What am I?
A bull does me, a battery holds me, and the police press me. What am I?
Bowlers want me, batters fear me, and workers walk out on me. What am I?
I hold fish, I roll into battle, and I'm a shirt with no sleeves. What am I?
I lift your car, I'm in a deck of cards, and headphones plug into me. What am I?
I'm the last words written about you, carved rather than spoken. What am I?
I'm a road that promises to take you somewhere, then gives up. What am I?
I'm called the lowest form of humor, and I make people groan on purpose. What am I?
I'm what you say when you're okay, and what you pay when you park where you shouldn't. What am I?
I hit tennis balls, and I'm also a shady scheme for making money. What am I?
I sound exactly like another word but mean something completely different. What am I?
